metadata.note: Two mainlines that met at Nashville Union Station (opened 1900, jointly built and owned by the L&N and NC&StL, the two companies that dominated Nashville rail traffic): the Louisville & Nashville Railroad's original namesake line north to Louisville (completed 1859), and the Nashville, Chattanooga & St. Louis Railway's original line southeast to Chattanooga (the first railroad to operate in Tennessee, completed 1854). The NC&StL was taken over by the L&N in stages -- controlling stock interest in 1880, full corporate merger in 1957 -- but ran semi-independently in between. A third Nashville-area carrier, the Tennessee Central Railway, notably could not use Union Station (L&N/NC&StL controlled it) and is not included in this file. GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: both lines traced through real track geometry using OpenStreetMap data (Overpass API) and a shortest-path graph search chaining real way segments together, following the still-active CSX freight alignments that largely preserve the original 19th-century routes (Louisville-Elizabethtown-Bowling Green-Nashville for the L&N; Nashville-Murfreesboro-Tullahoma-Cowan-Bridgeport-Chattanooga for the NC&StL, including the famous Cowan grade over the Cumberland Plateau). Traced lengths (300.1 km / 186.5 mi for Louisville-Nashville, 244.3 km / 151.8 mi for Nashville-Chattanooga) closely match the historically documented mileages (~180 mi and 152 mi respectively), corroborating the routing. Frequencies (headway_min) are estimated/unsourced except where a specific train count or 'single daily' schedule is cited in a segment note. Also includes the NC&StL's Paducah & Memphis Division, the through Nashville-Memphis line (direct Memphis access from 1896), whose Dutchman's Curve single-track section in Belle Meade was the site of the Jul 9 1918 head-on collision that remains the deadliest rail accident in US history. Its geometry is hand-placed town waypoints rather than a modern alignment, since no passenger service remains; the points east of Bruceton (Dutchman's Curve, Dickson, Waverly, Johnsonville) are well attested, while those west of Bruceton toward Memphis are approximate. Note the L&N separately reached Memphis by its own Memphis-Clarksville-Guthrie route, which joined its Louisville main north of Nashville and is not drawn here. ACCURACY NOTE: the Nashville-Memphis waypoints as drawn total about 327 km, while the railroad's own Paducah & Memphis Division was roughly 254 miles (409 km). The real alignment was therefore noticeably less direct than this simplified path - sources describe it as semicircular - so treat the drawn shape as indicative of the corridor and its endpoints, not of the true mileage or curvature. Also includes the L&N's Memphis Branch (Memphis-Paris-Clarksville-Guthrie-Bowling Green), the separate, more northerly Memphis route that reached the L&N main at Bowling Green rather than running direct to Nashville. Geometry is hand-placed waypoints on the towns the sources name (Memphis, McKenzie, Paris, Clarksville, Guthrie, Bowling Green); no intermediate stations could be sourced for the long Memphis-McKenzie leg, so that stretch is drawn as a single straight line and understates the real alignment.

Its Bowling Green extension was completed Sept 16 1860, with the first regular through train Sept 24 1860. properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced from OpenStreetMap, replacing the 6-point straight-line sketch (Memphis - McKenzie - Paris - Clarksville - Guthrie - Bowling Green) that stood here before. Route: Memphis Union Station - Binghampton - Bartlett - Arlington - Stanton - Brownsville - Humboldt - Milan - McKenzie - Paris - Big Sandy - Danville (Tennessee River) - Erin - Cumberland City - Clarksville - Guthrie - Russellville - Bowling Green. 227 points, traced length 264.5 mi. Of the routed path, 246.3 mi lies on ways OSM tags old_railway_operator=L&N (the modern CSX Memphis Subdivision, the R.J. Corman Memphis Line, and the abandoned grade between Paris and Erin); 17.5 mi lies on untagged rail in the same corridor, chiefly the Memphis terminal approach and short stretches where the operator tag simply stops. MILEAGE CHECK against the L&N milepost list in branchline.uk's Tennessee (line 18, Guthrie - Memphis) and Kentucky (line 34, Bowling Green - Guthrie) station lists: Memphis Union Station MP 493.9 to Bowling Green MP 227.3 is a documented 266.6 mi; traced 264.8 mi, 0.7% short. Station-to-station the fit is close - Broad Street (Binghampton) to Guthrie documented 210.4 mi against 208.7 traced; Guthrie to Bowling Green documented 50.3 against 50.3; McKenzie - Paris 17.2 against 17.2; Humboldt - Milan 11.3 against 11.3; Brownsville - Humboldt 24.9 against 24.9. APPROXIMATED LEGS: three straight-line bridges totalling 0.95 mi (1.53 km) across the flooded Kentucky Lake embayments either side of Big Sandy, at traced miles 146.5 (0.14 km), 147.4 (0.42 km) and 148.9 (0.97 km) - these crossings went under water when Kentucky Dam was closed and no grade survives to trace. Nothing else on the line is straight-line: the remaining 263.6 mi all follows mapped track or mapped abandoned grade. ERA CAVEATS: (1) the drawn line reaches Memphis Union Station, which opened in 1912. For the 1859-1912 segments this is a later terminal than the trains actually used - the L&N station was at N. Main and Auction (MP 488), reached from the west bank by ferry until through service was diverted over the Frisco Bridge in 1892, and Central Station was used 1901-1912. The last 5.8 mi into Memphis is terminal trackage that the milepost book does not cover, so it is the least certain part of the trace. (2) between Big Sandy (MP 344.3) and Paris (MP 360.8) the branchline.uk list records a former alignment with a first-generation Springville and Porters about half a mile off the later mileposts; OSM maps one abandoned grade there and it is drawn as the line for every era, so the earliest years may be shown on the later of the two alignments.
